lessons.title: Nice to Meet You
lessons.goal: Greet someone you meet for the first time, give your name, and ask and say where people are from and what they do.
lessons.context: A cultural exchange party (こうりゅうかい). Kim, a student, meets Mr Inoue, an office worker, for the first time.

dialogue.speaker: キム
dialogue.ja: こんにちは。はじめまして。キムです。
dialogue.en: Hello. Nice to meet you. I’m Kim.

dialogue.speaker: いのうえ
dialogue.ja: あ、はじめまして。いのうえです。どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。
dialogue.en: Oh, nice to meet you. I’m Inoue. Pleased to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: キム
dialogue.ja: どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。いのうえさんは がくせいですか。
dialogue.en: Pleased to meet you. Are you a student, Mr Inoue?

dialogue.speaker: いのうえ
dialogue.ja: いいえ、がくせいじゃ ありません。かいしゃいんです。キムさんは？
dialogue.en: No, I’m not a student. I’m an office worker. And you, Kim?

dialogue.speaker: キム
dialogue.ja: わたしは がくせいです。にほんごがっこうの がくせいです。
dialogue.en: I’m a student. I’m a student at a Japanese language school.

dialogue.speaker: いのうえ
dialogue.ja: そうですか。あの ひとは だれですか。
dialogue.en: I see. Who is that person?

dialogue.speaker: キム
dialogue.ja: あおきせんせいです。にほんごがっこうの せんせいです。
dialogue.en: That’s Ms Aoki. She’s a teacher at the Japanese language school.

lessons.question: You meet someone at a party for the first time. Which line introduces you?
choices: はじめまして。キムです。
はじめまして。キムさんです。
feedback: はじめまして, then your own name with です.
さん goes after other people’s names, never your own.
This asks the other person about Kim; it does not introduce you.
lessons.focus: Introduce yourself and others with ［N1］は ［N2］です and こちらは ～さんです, add a second person with ～も, and ask ～ですか, answering はい or いいえ、～じゃ ありません. Ask about someone with あの ひとは だれですか.

words.frame: どうぞ よろしく おねがいします

sections.title: Saying who or what someone is
sections.pattern: ［N1］は ［N2］です。
sections.explain: は marks the topic, the person you are talking about, and ［N2］です says who or what they are: a name, a country or a job. To introduce the person beside you, say こちらは ［name］さんです.

examples.ja: わたしは タンです。
examples.en: I’m Tan.

examples.ja: サラさんは かいしゃいんです。
examples.en: Sara is an office worker.

examples.ja: こちらは キムさんです。
examples.en: This is Kim.

examples.ja: おくには どちらですか。― ベトナムです。
examples.en: Where are you from? — Vietnam.

sections.note: さん goes after other people’s names, never after your own. Your own job as a teacher is きょうし; a teacher you talk to or about is せんせい. の joins two nouns, the first describing the second: にほんごがっこうの がくせい is a student of the Japanese language school.

sections.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

items.explain: じん after a country makes a person from it, and ご its language: にほんじん, にほんご.

sections.instruction: Choose what the underlined part means here.

items.prompt: At the party, a woman comes up to you and says this. What does the underlined part mean?
items.ja: はじめまして。キムです。
feedback: はじめまして opens a first meeting, before your name.
“Excuse me” is すみません.
“I see” is そうですか.

items.prompt: Tan looks at a man by the window and asks Kim this. What does he want to know?
items.ja: あの ひとは だれですか。
choices: Whether that man is a student
feedback: だれ is “who”: Tan asks who the man is.
Where someone is from is asked with くに and どちら.
That would be がくせいですか.

items.prompt: Sara asks Tan this at the party. What is she asking?
items.ja: おくには どちらですか。
feedback: くに is country, and どちら asks which one: she asks where he is from.
A job is しごと.
“Who” is だれ.

items.prompt: At the party, Kim tells you about the woman by the window. What does the underlined part mean?
items.ja: あの ひとは にほんごの せんせいです。
items.mark: にほんごの せんせい
choices: A Japanese person who is a teacher
feedback: の joins the two nouns: にほんご says what kind of teacher she is.
With の, the two nouns make one thing, a teacher of Japanese, not two separate things.
にほんご is the language; a Japanese person is にほんじん.

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each sentence.

items.ja: わたし（　） タンです。
items.en: I’m Tan.
feedback: は marks わたし as the person you are talking about.
も means “too”, but nobody has been named before you.
か makes a question; it does not follow わたし.

items.ja: サラさんは かいしゃいん（　）。
items.en: Sara is an office worker.
feedback: です ends the sentence: Sara is an office worker.
さん goes after a name, not after a job.
じん goes after a country, not after a job.

items.ja: こちらは キム（　）です。
items.en: This is Kim.
feedback: You are introducing Kim, so her name takes さん.
は is already after こちら; the name still needs さん.
じん goes after a country: にほんじん.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: Sara is an office worker.
items.explain: The person with は, then what she is, then です.

items.en: This is Mr Inoue.
items.explain: こちらは presents the person beside you; わたしは would make you Inoue.

sections.instruction: Choose what you would say.

items.prompt: You are Kim. You meet Tan for the first time at the party. What do you say first?
choices: はじめまして。キムです。
はじめまして。キムさんです。
あの ひとは キムです。
feedback: はじめまして, then your own name with です.
さん is for other people’s names, never your own.
あの ひと is “that person”: this talks about someone else.

items.prompt: Ms Nakamura is standing next to you. You introduce her to Sara. What do you say?
choices: こちらは なかむらさんです。
わたしは なかむらさんです。
あの ひとは なかむらです。
feedback: こちらは points politely to the person beside you.
わたしは would say that you are Nakamura.
あの ひと is someone over there, and her name needs さん.

sections.title: Saying “too” with も
sections.pattern: ［N1］は ［A］です。［N2］も ［A］です。
sections.explain: When a second person is the same, も takes the place of は: “［N2］ too”. The rest of the sentence stays the same.

examples.ja: タンさんは がくせいです。キムさんも がくせいです。
examples.en: Tan is a student. Kim is a student too.

examples.ja: サラさんは かいしゃいんです。わたしも かいしゃいんです。
examples.en: Sara is an office worker. I’m an office worker too.

sections.note: If the second person is different, keep は: キムさんは がくせいです。サラさんは かいしゃいんです。

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each pair of sentences.

items.ja: タンさんは だいがくせいです。ラマさん（　） だいがくせいです。
items.en: Tan is a university student. Lama is a university student too.
feedback: も says Lama is a university student too, like Tan.
は would state it as a separate fact; the English says “too”.
か would turn it into a question.

items.ja: キムさんは がくせいです。サラさん（　） かいしゃいんです。
items.en: Kim is a student. Sara is an office worker.
feedback: Sara’s job is different from Kim’s, so she takes は.
も says “too”, but Sara is not a student like Kim.

items.ja: あおきせんせいは にほんじんです。なかむらさんも （　）。
items.en: Ms Aoki is Japanese. Ms Nakamura is Japanese too.
feedback: After も the sentence repeats what is the same: にほんじん.
も means the same thing again, so it cannot bring in a new job.
にほんご is the language; a person is にほんじん.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: I’m a university student too.
items.explain: も goes where は would go, straight after わたし.

sections.instruction: Choose your reply.

items.prompt: Tan says: わたしは ベトナムじんです。 You are Vietnamese too. What do you say?
choices: わたしも ベトナムじんです。
わたしは ベトナムじんですか。
わたしも ベトナムです。
feedback: も adds you: you are Vietnamese too.
か turns it into a question about yourself.
A person is ベトナムじん; ベトナム is the country.

items.prompt: Sara says: わたしは かいしゃいんです。 You are a student. What do you say?
choices: わたしは がくせいです。
わたしも がくせいです。
わたしも かいしゃいんです。
feedback: Your job is different, so は: you are a student.
も would mean a student too, but Sara is not one.
This says you are an office worker too, which is not true.

sections.title: Asking yes–no questions, and who
sections.pattern: ［N1］は ［A］ですか。― はい、［A］です。／いいえ、［A］じゃ ありません。
sections.explain: Put か after です to make a question. Answer はい with the same word and です, or いいえ with じゃ ありません, then say what is right. To ask who someone is, use だれですか.

examples.ja: キムさんは がくせいですか。― はい、がくせいです。
examples.en: Is Kim a student? — Yes, she is.

examples.ja: サラさんは がくせいですか。― いいえ、がくせいじゃ ありません。かいしゃいんです。
examples.en: Is Sara a student? — No, she isn’t. She’s an office worker.

examples.ja: あの ひとは だれですか。― あおきせんせいです。
examples.en: Who is that person? — That’s Ms Aoki, the teacher.

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each line.

items.ja: キムさんは がくせいです（　）。
items.en: Is Kim a student?
feedback: か after です turns the sentence into a question.
も means “too”; it does not come after です.
は marks a topic; it cannot end a sentence.

items.ja: いいえ、きょうし（　）。がくせいです。
items.en: No, I’m not a teacher. I’m a student.
feedback: After いいえ, じゃ ありません says what you are not.
です would say you are a teacher, the opposite of いいえ.
ですか asks a question; this is an answer.

items.ja: あの ひとは （　）ですか。― いのうえさんです。
items.en: Who is that person? — Mr Inoue.
feedback: The answer is a name, so the question asks だれ, who.
がくせいですか is a yes–no question, but the answer is a name.
わたし is “I”; it does not ask anything.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: Is Sara a student?
items.explain: The person with は, the word you ask about, then ですか.

items.en: No, I’m not a student. I’m an office worker.
items.explain: いいえ first, then what you are not with じゃ ありません and what you are with です.

sections.instruction: Choose the best answer.

items.prompt: Tan asks: サラさんは がくせいですか。 Sara works for a company. What does she answer?
choices: いいえ、がくせいじゃ ありません。かいしゃいんです。
いいえ、かいしゃいんじゃ ありません。
feedback: Sara is not a student: いいえ, じゃ ありません, then her real job.
はい would say Sara is a student.
This denies that Sara is an office worker, which she is.

items.prompt: A man you don’t know is talking to Ms Aoki. You want Kim to tell you who he is. What do you ask?
choices: あの ひとは だれですか。
あの ひとは だれです。
わたしは だれですか。
feedback: だれですか asks who the man over there is.
Without か it is not a question.
わたしは だれですか asks who you are.

items.prompt: Kim asks: にほんの かたですか。 You are Japanese. What do you answer?
choices: いいえ、にほんじんです。
はい、にほんじんじゃ ありません。
feedback: はい, then what you are: a Japanese person.
いいえ does not fit with “I am Japanese” after it.
はい with じゃ ありません says yes and no at once.

sections.instruction: Mark each statement ○ (true) or × (false).

items.statement: Mr Inoue is a student.
items.explain: He says がくせいじゃ ありません: he is an office worker.

items.statement: Kim is a student at a Japanese language school.
items.explain: Kim says にほんごがっこうの がくせいです.

items.statement: Mr Inoue already knows who the teacher is.
items.explain: He asks あの ひとは だれですか, so he does not know her yet.

sections.instruction: Complete the new conversation with words from the box.

lines.speaker: タン
lines.ja: サラさん、こちらは ラマさんです。

lines.speaker: ラマ
lines.ja: はじめまして。ラマです。どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。

lines.speaker: サラ
lines.ja: サラです。どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。ラマさんは （1）ですか。

lines.speaker: ラマ
lines.ja: はい、がくせいです。

lines.speaker: サラ
lines.ja: タンさん（2） がくせいですか。

lines.speaker: ラマ
lines.ja: はい。サラさんは？

lines.speaker: サラ
lines.ja: わたしは がくせい（3）。かいしゃいんです。あの ひとは （4）ですか。

lines.speaker: ラマ
lines.ja: なかむらさんです。

items.en: Sara, this is Lama. — Nice to meet you. I’m Lama. — I’m Sara. Pleased to meet you. Are you a student? — Yes, I am. — Is Tan a student too? — Yes. And you? — I’m not a student. I’m an office worker. Who is that person? — Ms Nakamura.
items.explain: Ask about a job with ですか, add Tan with も, deny with じゃ ありません and ask who with だれ.

sections.instruction: Use everything from this lesson.

items.en: I’m not an office worker.
items.explain: じゃ ありません comes straight after the word you deny.

items.prompt: Lama is a student, and so is Kim. Which pair of sentences says that?
choices: ラマさんは がくせいです。キムさんも がくせいです。
ラマさんも がくせいです。キムさんは がくせいです。
ラマさんは がくせいです。キムさんは がくせいですか。
feedback: は for the first person, も for the second: Kim too.
も belongs to the second person, after the first is said with は.
The second sentence asks a question instead of saying it.

items.prompt: Someone asks: タンさんは かいしゃいんですか。 Tan is a university student. What does Tan answer?
choices: いいえ、かいしゃいんじゃ ありません。だいがくせいです。
はい、だいがくせいです。
いいえ、だいがくせいじゃ ありません。
feedback: いいえ to deny the job he was asked about, then what he really is.
はい answers yes to かいしゃいんですか, which is wrong.
This denies being a university student, which he is.

items.en: Excuse me. Who is that person?
items.explain: すみません gets attention, then the person with は and だれですか.

items.prompt: You have said はじめまして and your name to Mr Inoue. What do you say to end your introduction?
choices: どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。
あの ひとは だれですか。
feedback: どうぞ よろしく おねがいします closes a first introduction.
そうですか reacts to news: “I see”.
This asks about someone else.

items.prompt: Tan tells you: わたしは ベトナムじんです。 You did not know that. What do you reply?
choices: どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。
feedback: そうですか takes in news you have just heard: “I see”.
You have already met; はじめまして is only for the start.
This closes an introduction; it does not react to news.

occurrences.surface: どうぞ よろしく おねがいします
どうぞ よろしく おねがいします

lessons.title: Nice Weather Today
lessons.goal: Greet the neighbours at any time of day, make small talk about the weather, and ask someone to say it again.
lessons.context: Outside an apartment building on a cold evening. Sara, who works for a company, meets her neighbour Mr Nishikawa on her way home.

dialogue.speaker: にしかわ
dialogue.ja: こんばんは。
dialogue.en: Good evening.

dialogue.speaker: サラ
dialogue.ja: こんばんは。さむいですね。
dialogue.en: Good evening. It’s cold, isn’t it?

dialogue.speaker: にしかわ
dialogue.ja: そうですね。おしごとですか。
dialogue.en: It is. Have you been at work?

dialogue.speaker: サラ
dialogue.ja: え？ すみません。ゆっくり おねがいします。
dialogue.en: Sorry? Slowly, please.

dialogue.speaker: にしかわ
dialogue.ja: おしごと、ですか。
dialogue.en: (slowly) At work?

dialogue.speaker: サラ
dialogue.ja: あ、はい、そうです。
dialogue.en: Oh, yes, that’s right.

dialogue.speaker: にしかわ
dialogue.ja: そうですか。おつかれさまでした。
dialogue.en: I see. Well done today.

dialogue.speaker: サラ
dialogue.ja: ありがとうございます。おやすみなさい。
dialogue.en: Thank you. Good night.

dialogue.speaker: にしかわ
dialogue.ja: おやすみなさい。
dialogue.en: Good night.

lessons.question: You leave home for school, and your host mother stays at home. Which pair do you and she say?
choices: いってきます。― いってらっしゃい。
いってらっしゃい。― いってきます。
おやすみなさい。― こんばんは。
feedback: The one leaving says いってきます; the one staying answers いってらっしゃい.
These are swapped: you are the one leaving.
These are evening and bedtime words, not for leaving home.
lessons.focus: Greet people for the time of day and the moment, make small talk with いい てんきですね ― そうですね, and ask someone to repeat with もう いちど おねがいします or ゆっくり おねがいします.

words.frame: いい てんきですね
もう いちど おねがいします

sections.title: Greetings for the time and the moment
sections.pattern: おはようございます・こんにちは・こんばんは
sections.explain: Choose the greeting by the time of day: おはようございます in the morning, こんにちは in the daytime and こんばんは in the evening. Leaving home, say いってきます; the person staying says いってらっしゃい. Leaving work before others, say しつれいします; they answer おつかれさまでした.

examples.ja: おはようございます。― おはようございます。
examples.en: Good morning. — Good morning.

examples.ja: いってきます。― いってらっしゃい。
examples.en: I’m off. — See you later.

examples.ja: しつれいします。― おつかれさまでした。
examples.en: I’ll be going. — Thanks for your work today.

examples.ja: おやすみなさい。
examples.en: Good night.

sections.note: すみません calls someone over, thanks them for trouble or apologises; ごめんなさい only apologises, mostly to family and friends.

sections.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

items.explain: あつい and さむい describe the weather, as in あついですね.

sections.instruction: Choose the greeting that fits.

items.prompt: It is eight in the morning. You meet Mr Nishikawa outside your building. What do you say?
feedback: Eight in the morning: おはようございます.
こんばんは is for the evening.
おやすみなさい is for bedtime.

items.prompt: You leave home for school. Your host mother is staying at home. What do you say?
feedback: You are leaving and coming back: いってきます.
いってらっしゃい is what your host mother says to you.
さようなら sounds like a long goodbye, not leaving for the day.

items.prompt: At seven in the evening you meet Mr Tanaka at the station. What do you say?
feedback: Seven in the evening: こんばんは.
おはようございます is for the morning.
こんにちは is for the daytime; it is evening now.

sections.instruction: Choose the best reply.

items.prompt: Your coworker leaves the office before you and says しつれいします. What do you answer?
feedback: A coworker finishing for the day gets おつかれさまでした.
いってらっしゃい sends someone off who will come back soon.
ごめんなさい apologises; nobody has done anything wrong.

items.prompt: A neighbour hands you a parcel that came for you while you were out. What do you say?
choices: ありがとうございます。
feedback: She did you a favour, so you thank her.
どうぞ is what you say when you hand something over.
さようなら is goodbye, not thanks.

items.prompt: On a crowded train, your bag bumps into a stranger. What do you say?
feedback: すみません apologises to a stranger for the bump.
どうぞ offers something or lets someone go first.
おやすみなさい is for bedtime.

sections.title: Small talk about the weather
sections.pattern: いい てんきですね。― そうですね。
sections.explain: ね invites the other person to agree about something you both can see or feel. The usual reply is そうですね, “yes, it is”. Say the weather the same way: あめですね, あついですね, さむいですね.

examples.ja: いい てんきですね。― そうですね。
examples.en: Nice weather, isn’t it? — Yes, it is.

examples.ja: あついですね。― そうですね。
examples.en: It’s hot, isn’t it? — Yes, it is.

examples.ja: あめですね。
examples.en: It’s raining, isn’t it?

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each line.

items.ja: いい てんき（　）。
items.en: Nice weather, isn’t it?
feedback: ですね invites your neighbour to agree about the fine weather.
ですか asks a question, but you both can see the weather.
じゃ ありません would say it is not nice weather.

items.ja: あついですね。―（　）。
items.en: It’s hot, isn’t it? — Yes, it is.
feedback: そうですね agrees about the heat you both feel.
そうですか takes in news; the heat is not news.
はじめまして is only for a first meeting.

items.ja: （　）ですね。
items.en: It’s cold, isn’t it?
feedback: さむい is cold weather.
あつい is the opposite: hot.
あめ is rain, not cold.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: Nice weather, isn’t it?
items.explain: いい before てんき, then ですね to invite agreement.

sections.instruction: Choose the best answer.

items.prompt: On a cold morning, Mr Nishikawa says: さむいですね。 What do you answer?
choices: ありがとうございます。
feedback: そうですね agrees that it is cold.
いいえ does not fit with agreeing that it is cold.
He has not given you anything to thank him for.

items.prompt: It is pouring with rain as you meet a neighbour at the door. Which small talk fits?
choices: いい てんきですね。
feedback: あめですね talks about the rain you both can see.
It is raining, so it is not fine weather.
おやすみなさい is for bedtime, not small talk.

sections.title: Asking someone to say it again
sections.pattern: もう いちど おねがいします。／ゆっくり おねがいします。
sections.explain: When you miss what someone said, say すみません, then もう いちど おねがいします, “once more, please”. If they spoke too fast, ask ゆっくり おねがいします; えいごで おねがいします asks for English.

examples.ja: え？ すみません。もう いちど おねがいします。
examples.en: Huh? Sorry, once more, please.

examples.ja: すみません。ゆっくり おねがいします。
examples.en: Sorry, slowly, please.

examples.ja: すみません。えいごで おねがいします。
examples.en: Sorry, in English, please.

sections.note: When someone checks what you said, はい、そうです answers “yes, that’s right”.

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each request.

items.ja: すみません。もう （　） おねがいします。
items.en: Sorry, once more, please.
feedback: もう いちど is “one more time”.
ゆっくり is “slowly”; it does not follow もう.
えいご is English; it does not follow もう.

items.ja: すみません。（　） おねがいします。
items.en: Sorry, slowly, please.
feedback: ゆっくり asks for slower speech.
いちど needs もう in front: もう いちど.
そうです means “that’s right”; it asks for nothing.

items.ja: すみません。えいご（　） おねがいします。
items.en: Sorry, in English, please.
feedback: えいごで asks them to say it in English.
は would make English the topic; the request needs で.
も would mean “English too”.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: Sorry, slowly, please.
items.explain: すみません first, then ゆっくり and おねがいします.

sections.instruction: Choose what you would say.

items.prompt: You understand Japanese, but your neighbour is speaking very fast. What do you ask?
choices: ゆっくり おねがいします。
えいごで おねがいします。
feedback: The problem is speed, so you ask for ゆっくり.
You understand Japanese; only the speed is the problem.
いってらっしゃい sends someone off.

items.prompt: A neighbour asks you something, and you do not catch it at all. What do you say?
choices: え？ すみません。もう いちど おねがいします。
feedback: You missed it, so you ask for it once more.
そうですね agrees with something you have not understood.
いってらっしゃい sends someone off.

items.prompt: She says it again slowly: がっこうですか。 You are on your way to school. What do you answer?
feedback: はい、そうです: yes, that’s right, to school.
そうですか takes in news; she asked you a question.
いいえ and そうです say no and yes at once.

sections.instruction: Mark each statement ○ (true) or × (false).

items.statement: Sara meets Mr Nishikawa in the morning.
items.explain: They say こんばんは: it is the evening.

items.statement: Sara asks Mr Nishikawa to speak more slowly.
items.explain: She says ゆっくり おねがいします.

items.statement: They both find it cold.
items.explain: Sara says さむいですね, and he agrees with そうですね.

sections.instruction: Complete the new conversation with words from the box.

lines.speaker: タン
lines.ja: おはようございます。いい てんきですね。

lines.speaker: たなか
lines.ja: （2）。がっこうですか。

lines.speaker: タン
lines.ja: はい、そうです。（3）。

items.en: Good morning. — Good morning. Nice weather, isn’t it? — Yes, it is. Off to school? — Yes. I’m off. — See you later.
items.explain: A morning greeting, agreement with そうですね, then いってきます from the one leaving and いってらっしゃい from the one staying.

sections.instruction: Use everything from this lesson.

items.en: Sorry, in English, please.
items.explain: で after えいご says the language you want.

items.prompt: At nine at night, your host family’s child goes to bed. What do you say?
feedback: Going to bed: おやすみなさい.
こんばんは greets someone in the evening; it is not for bedtime.
さようなら is a goodbye for parting, not for bedtime at home.

items.prompt: Class is over and you leave your teacher at the school gate. What do you say?
feedback: At the end of school you part with さようなら.
いってきます is for leaving home.
おはようございます is for the morning.

items.prompt: A little boy has broken his mother’s cup. What does he say to her?
feedback: A child apologising to his mother says ごめんなさい.
どうぞ hands something over.
おつかれさまでした thanks someone for their work.

items.en: Huh? Sorry. Once more, please.
items.explain: え？ shows you missed it, すみません apologises, then the request.

items.prompt: On a hot summer evening you meet a neighbour. Which pair fits?
choices: こんばんは。あついですね。
おはようございます。あついですね。
こんばんは。さむいですね。
feedback: An evening greeting, then small talk about the heat.
おはようございます is for the morning.
It is hot, not cold.

lessons.title: New Next Door
lessons.goal: Greet a new neighbour when you move in, say when and where you came from, and offer a small gift.
lessons.context: Moving-in greetings (ひっこしの あいさつ). Shin has just moved into room 203 and visits his neighbour Mr Nishikawa with a small gift.

dialogue.speaker: シン
dialogue.ja: こんにちは。はじめまして。203の シンです。どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。
dialogue.en: Hello. Nice to meet you. I’m Shin from 203. Pleased to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: にしかわ
dialogue.ja: あ、はじめまして。にしかわです。よろしく おねがいします。おくには どちらですか。
dialogue.en: Oh, nice to meet you. I’m Nishikawa. Pleased to meet you. Where are you from?

dialogue.speaker: シン
dialogue.ja: インドです。せんしゅう ムンバイから きました。
dialogue.en: India. I came from Mumbai last week.

dialogue.speaker: にしかわ
dialogue.ja: ああ、そうですか。
dialogue.en: Ah, I see.

dialogue.speaker: シン
dialogue.ja: あのう、にしかわさんは あまい ものを たべますか。
dialogue.en: Um, do you eat sweet things, Mr Nishikawa?

dialogue.speaker: にしかわ
dialogue.ja: はい、たべます。すきです。
dialogue.en: Yes, I do. I like them.

dialogue.speaker: シン
dialogue.ja: これ、インドの チョコレートです。どうぞ。
dialogue.en: This is chocolate from India. Please, have it.

dialogue.speaker: にしかわ
dialogue.ja: わあ、ありがとうございます。
dialogue.en: Oh, wow, thank you.

lessons.question: Your new neighbour asks when you came to Japan. You came last year. What do you answer?
choices: きょねん きました。
きょねんから きました。
きょねんへ きました。
feedback: きょねん takes no particle: きょねん きました.
から marks a place you came from, not a time.
へ marks a place you came to, not a time.
lessons.focus: Say where you came from with ［N］は ［place］から きました and when with いつ … きましたか, and ask about food and drink with ［N］を のみますか／たべますか, answering ～ます or ～ません.

sections.title: Where you came from
sections.pattern: ［N］は ［place］から きました。
sections.explain: から marks the place you came from, and きました means “came”. To ask where someone is from, say おくには どちらですか; ［country］の どちらですか asks which part.

examples.ja: わたしは ベトナムから きました。
examples.en: I came from Vietnam.

examples.ja: おくには どちらですか。― ネパールです。
examples.en: Where are you from? — Nepal.

examples.ja: ネパールの どちらですか。― カトマンズです。
examples.en: Where in Nepal? — Kathmandu.

sections.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

items.explain: のみます goes with drinks and たべます with food.

sections.instruction: Choose what the underlined word shows here.

items.prompt: You hand your new neighbour a gift, and she says this. What does the underlined word show?
items.ja: わあ、ありがとうございます。
feedback: わあ is a happy “wow” at the gift.
An apology would be すみません or ごめんなさい.
Not hearing would be え？

items.prompt: Tan wants to ask his neighbour something and begins like this. What does the underlined word do?
items.ja: あのう、たなかさんは ワインを のみますか。
feedback: あのう starts a question softly, a little hesitantly.
A goodbye would be さようなら.
Agreeing would be そうですね.

items.prompt: The neighbour learns where Tan is from and says this. What does the underlined word show?
items.ja: ああ、そうですか。
choices: He is surprised by a gift.
feedback: ああ with そうですか shows he has taken in the news.
A happy surprise at a gift is わあ.
Missing something is え？

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each line.

items.ja: わたしは ネパール（　） きました。
items.en: I came from Nepal.
feedback: から marks Nepal as where you came from.
へ would mean you came to Nepal.
を marks what you drink or eat, not a place.

items.ja: おくには （　）ですか。
items.en: Where are you from?
feedback: どちら asks which country.
だれ asks who; くに is a country.
これ is “this”; it does not ask anything.

items.ja: インドネシア（　） どちらですか。― ジャカルタです。
items.en: Where in Indonesia? — Jakarta.
feedback: の どちら asks which part of Indonesia.
から どちら does not ask a place inside the country.
インドネシアは どちらですか asks where Indonesia is.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: I came from Ho Chi Minh City.
items.explain: The place, then から, then きました.

sections.instruction: Choose what you would say.

items.prompt: A neighbour asks: おくには どちらですか。 You are from India. What do you answer?
choices: インドから きましたか。
インドの どちらですか。
feedback: The country with です answers the question.
This asks her a question back.
This asks which part of India.

items.prompt: Tan says he is from Vietnam. You want to know which city. What do you ask?
choices: ベトナムの どちらですか。
ベトナムから きましたか。
おくには どちらですか。
feedback: の どちら asks which part of Vietnam.
He has already said he is from Vietnam.
He has already told you his country.

sections.title: When you came
sections.pattern: いつ ［place］へ きましたか。― ［time］（に） きました。
sections.explain: いつ asks when, and へ marks the place someone came to. Answer with the time: せんしゅう and きょねん take no particle, but a month takes に, as in 1がつに きました.

examples.ja: サラさんは いつ にほんへ きましたか。― せんしゅう きました。
examples.en: When did Sara come to Japan? — She came last week.

examples.ja: わたしは 3がつに きました。
examples.en: I came in March.

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each line.

items.ja: いつ にほん（　） きましたか。
items.en: When did you come to Japan?
feedback: へ marks Japan as where you came to.
から would ask when you came from Japan.
を marks what you drink or eat.

items.ja: わたしは 1がつ（　） きました。
items.en: I came in January.
feedback: A month takes に: 1がつに.
へ marks a place you go to, not a time.
を marks what you drink or eat.

items.ja: いつ にほんへ きましたか。―（　） きました。
items.en: — I came last week.
feedback: せんしゅう is last week.
きょねん is last year.
ベトナムから says where, but いつ asks when.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: When did you come to Japan?
items.explain: いつ and the place can come in either order; きましたか comes last.

sections.instruction: Choose the best answer.

items.prompt: Kim came to Japan in January. How does she say so?
feedback: A month takes に.
から marks where you came from, not when.
を marks what you drink or eat.

items.prompt: A neighbour asks when you came. You came last year. What do you say?
choices: きょねん きました。
せんしゅう きました。
きょねんから きました。
feedback: きょねん, with no particle, then きました.
せんしゅう is last week.
から marks a place you came from.

sections.title: Do you drink it? Do you eat it?
sections.pattern: ［N］を のみます／のみません／のみますか。
sections.explain: を marks what you drink or eat. ～ます says you do it, ～ません that you don’t, and ～ますか asks. Answer with the same verb: はい、のみます or いいえ、のみません.

examples.ja: たなかさんは ビールを のみますか。― はい、のみます。
examples.en: Do you drink beer, Mr Tanaka? — Yes, I do.

examples.ja: わたしは おさけを のみません。
examples.en: I don’t drink alcohol.

examples.ja: ラマさんは ケーキを たべますか。― いいえ、たべません。
examples.en: Do you eat cake, Lama? — No, I don’t.

sections.note: Add すきです to say you like it: はい、のみます。すきです。

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each line.

items.ja: たなかさんは コーヒー（　） のみますか。
items.en: Do you drink coffee, Mr Tanaka?
feedback: を marks the coffee he drinks.
から marks a place you came from.
へ marks a place you go to.

items.ja: いいえ、わたしは しょうちゅうを （　）。
items.en: No, I don’t drink shochu.
feedback: いいえ, then のみません: you don’t drink it.
のみます says you do drink it.
のみますか would ask, not answer.

items.ja: キムさんは チョコレートを （　）か。
items.en: Does Kim eat chocolate?
feedback: Chocolate is food, so たべます.
のみます is for drinks.
きました is “came”; it does not take chocolate.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: No, I don’t eat sweets.
items.explain: いいえ, what you eat with を, then たべません.

sections.instruction: Choose the best answer.

items.prompt: You give your new neighbour Vietnamese coffee. What do you say as you hand it over?
choices: これ、ベトナムの コーヒーです。どうぞ。
これ、ベトナムの コーヒーですか。どうぞ。
コーヒーを のみません。どうぞ。
feedback: これ points to the gift, and どうぞ hands it over.
ですか asks what the gift is, which you know.
This says nobody drinks coffee, then offers it.

items.prompt: Mr Tanaka asks: ビールを のみますか。 You don’t drink alcohol. What do you answer?
feedback: いいえ with のみません: you don’t drink it.
はい does not go with のみません here.
いいえ and のみます say no and yes at once.

items.prompt: Lama asks: ケーキを たべますか。 You eat cake and like it. What do you answer?
choices: はい、たべます。すきです。
はい、のみます。すきです。
いいえ、たべません。すきです。
feedback: はい、たべます, and すきです adds that you like it.
Cake is eaten, not drunk.
たべません says you don’t eat it.

sections.instruction: Mark each statement ○ (true) or × (false).

items.statement: Shin came from Mumbai last year.
items.explain: He says せんしゅう: last week.

items.statement: Mr Nishikawa likes sweet things.
items.explain: He says はい、たべます。すきです。

items.statement: Shin gives Mr Nishikawa coffee.
items.explain: The gift is チョコレート, chocolate.

sections.instruction: Complete the new conversation with words from the box.

lines.speaker: キム
lines.ja: はじめまして。102の キムです。ソウル（1） きました。

lines.speaker: たなか
lines.ja: たなかです。いつ にほん（2） きましたか。

lines.speaker: キム
lines.ja: 3がつ（3） きました。あのう、たなかさんは ワインを （4）。

lines.speaker: たなか
lines.ja: はい、のみます。すきです。

items.en: Nice to meet you. I’m Kim from 102. I came from Seoul. — I’m Tanaka. When did you come to Japan? — In March. Um, do you drink wine? — Yes, I do. I like it.
items.explain: から for where she came from, へ for where she came to, に after a month, and のみますか for wine.

sections.instruction: Use everything from this lesson.

items.prompt: You are Lama, a student, and you have just moved in. Which line introduces you to your neighbour?
choices: はじめまして。わたしは ラマです。がくせいです。
はじめまして。わたしは ラマさんです。がくせいです。
はじめまして。わたしも ラマです。がくせいです。
feedback: わたしは, your name and です, then your job.
さん never goes after your own name.
も means “too”; nobody else is Lama.

items.en: Lama came from Nepal last year.
items.explain: から marks Nepal as where Lama came from; the time comes first.

items.prompt: Your neighbour asks: おさけを のみますか。 You drink it and like it. What do you answer?
choices: はい、のみます。すきです。
feedback: はい、のみます, then すきです.
いいえ does not go with のみます.
おさけ is a drink, not food.

items.en: Um, do you eat cookies?
items.explain: あのう opens gently, then what you eat with を and たべますか.

items.prompt: You want to know when Sara came to Japan. What do you ask?
choices: サラさんは いつ にほんへ きましたか。
サラさんは にほんから きましたか。
サラさんは いつですか。
feedback: いつ, the place with へ, then きましたか.
This asks whether she came from Japan.
This does not say what you want to know about.

items.prompt: A new neighbour hands you a box and says: これ、どうぞ。 What do you say?
choices: わあ、ありがとうございます。
feedback: A happy わあ, then thanks for the gift.
Nobody offered you a drink.
This answers a when question nobody asked.

occurrences.surface: どうぞ よろしく おねがいします
よろしく おねがいします
ありがとうございます

lessons.title: This One, Please
lessons.goal: Tell a clerk what you want and how many, and ask the price.
lessons.context: A hamburger shop counter (ハンバーガーショップ). Tan orders from the menu board behind the clerk and checks the total.

dialogue.speaker: てんいん
dialogue.ja: いらっしゃいませ。
dialogue.en: Welcome.

dialogue.speaker: タン
dialogue.ja: すみません。あれは いくらですか。
dialogue.en: Excuse me. How much is that one, up there?

dialogue.speaker: てんいん
dialogue.ja: ハンバーガーですか。210えんです。
dialogue.en: The hamburger? It’s 210 yen.

dialogue.speaker: タン
dialogue.ja: じゃあ、ハンバーガーを ください。
dialogue.en: Okay, hamburgers, please.

dialogue.speaker: てんいん
dialogue.ja: はい。いくつですか。
dialogue.en: Certainly. How many?

dialogue.speaker: タン
dialogue.ja: みっつ ください。あ、ポテトを ひとつと コーラを ふたつ ください。
dialogue.en: Three, please. Oh, and one fries and two colas, please.

dialogue.speaker: てんいん
dialogue.ja: はい。ぜんぶで 950えんです。
dialogue.en: Certainly. That’s 950 yen altogether.

dialogue.speaker: タン
dialogue.ja: え？ すみません。もう いちど おねがいします。
dialogue.en: Sorry? Excuse me, once more, please.

dialogue.speaker: てんいん
dialogue.ja: 950えんです。
dialogue.en: 950 yen.

dialogue.speaker: タン
dialogue.ja: はい。
dialogue.en: Here you are.

lessons.question: The clerk asks: いくつですか。 You want two. What do you answer?
feedback: ふたつ is how many, and ください asks for them.
えん goes after a price, not after a count.
ですか asks a question back; the clerk wants your answer.
lessons.focus: Ask the price with いくらですか and point things out with これ, それ and あれ. Count with ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ … and order with ［N］を ［number］ ください.

sections.title: Asking the price
sections.pattern: ［N］は いくらですか。― ［number］えんです。
sections.explain: いくら asks how much something costs. Answer with the price and えん, then です. ぜんぶで in front of the price gives the total.

examples.ja: コーラは いくらですか。― 150えんです。
examples.en: How much is a cola? — 150 yen.

examples.ja: ぜんぶで いくらですか。― 1,200えんです。
examples.en: How much is it altogether? — 1,200 yen.

sections.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

items.explain: Most foreign food words are written in katakana; りんご, みず and こうちゃ are Japanese words, written in hiragana.

sections.instruction: Choose what the underlined part means here.

items.prompt: You walk into a hamburger shop, and the clerk says this. What does it mean?
items.ja: いらっしゃいませ。
feedback: いらっしゃいませ greets a customer coming in; you do not say it back.
“Thank you” is ありがとうございます.
“Excuse me” is すみません.

items.prompt: After your order, the clerk says this. What does the underlined part mean?
items.ja: ぜんぶで 640えんです。
feedback: ぜんぶで gives the total: 640 yen for everything.
The price is for the whole order, not one item.
ぜんぶで adds everything up; it is not a price per item.

items.prompt: Kim hears the prices and points at a cola. What does the underlined part mean?
items.ja: じゃあ、これに します。
feedback: に します after これ says she will take it.
The price question is これは いくらですか.
に します is a choice for, not against, this one.

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each line.

items.ja: すみません。ハンバーガーは （　）ですか。
items.en: Excuse me. How much is a hamburger?
feedback: いくら asks the price of the hamburger.
どちら asks which or where, not how much.
だれ asks who; a hamburger is not a person.

items.ja: コロッケは 120（　）です。
items.en: Croquettes are 120 yen.
feedback: えん after 120 makes it a price in yen.
さん goes after a person’s name, not a number.
じん goes after a country: にほんじん.

items.ja: （　） 520えんです。
items.en: That’s 520 yen altogether.
feedback: ぜんぶで before the price makes it the total.
じゃあ starts a decision; it does not add up a price.
いらっしゃいませ welcomes a customer at the door.

sections.instruction: Choose the best answer.

items.prompt: Tan asks the clerk: ポテトは いくらですか。 Look at the menu. What does the clerk answer?
feedback: The menu gives the fries at 150 yen, so 150えんです.
280 yen is the cheeseburger.
いくら asks a price, so the answer is a number with えん.

sections.title: This one, that one, which one
sections.pattern: これ・それ・あれ・どれ
sections.explain: これ is a thing near you, それ a thing near the person you are talking to, and あれ a thing away from you both. どれ asks which one. Each stands alone in place of the thing: これは いくらですか.

examples.ja: これは いくらですか。― それは 500えんです。
examples.en: How much is this? — That’s 500 yen.

examples.ja: あれは いくらですか。― あれは 2,000えんです。
examples.en: How much is that one over there? — That one is 2,000 yen.

examples.ja: どれですか。― それです。
examples.en: Which one? — That one, by you.

examples.ja: じゃあ、これに します。
examples.en: Okay, I’ll take this one.

sections.note: When you ask about the thing in your hand with これ, the clerk answers with それ.

sections.instruction: Choose what each person says.

items.prompt: You are holding a cup and want to know its price. What do you ask the clerk?
choices: これは いくらですか。
それは いくらですか。
あれは いくらですか。
feedback: The cup is in your hand, near you, so これ.
それ is a thing near the clerk, not in your hand.
あれ is a thing away from you both.

items.prompt: The clerk is holding a bag, and you ask about it. What do you say?
choices: それは いくらですか。
これは いくらですか。
あれは いくらですか。
feedback: The bag is near the clerk, the person you are talking to, so それ.
これ would be a thing near you.
The bag is close to the clerk, not away from you both.

items.prompt: You hold up a shirt and ask: これは いくらですか。 What does the clerk answer?
feedback: The shirt is in your hand, near you, so for the clerk it is それ.
これ would be a shirt near the clerk.
あれ would be a shirt away from you both.

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each line.

items.ja: ドーナッツを ひとつ ください。― はい。（　）ですか。
items.en: One donut, please. — Sure. Which one?
feedback: There are many donuts, so the clerk asks どれ, which one.
これ would point to one donut, not ask which.
いくら asks the price, not which one.

items.ja: じゃあ、これ（　） します。
items.en: Okay, I’ll take this one.
feedback: に before します marks this one as your choice.
を goes before ください, not before します here.
は makes これ a topic; the choice needs に.

items.ja: あのう、あれは いくらですか。― （　）は 3,000えんです。
items.en: Um, how much is that one over there? — That one is 3,000 yen.
feedback: The thing is away from both of you, so the clerk also says あれ.
これ would be something near the clerk.
それ would be something near you.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: (To the clerk, about the thing in front of her) How much is that?
items.explain: The thing is near the clerk, so それ, then いくらですか.

items.en: Okay, I’ll take that one over there.
items.explain: じゃあ starts the decision, and あれに します chooses the one away from you both.

sections.title: How many, and ordering
sections.pattern: ［N］を ［number］ ください。・［N1］と ［N2］を ください。
sections.explain: Count things with ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ, よっつ, いつつ, and ask how many with いくつですか. Put the number after を, just before ください. To order two things, join them with と, giving each its number: ［N1］を ひとつと ［N2］を ふたつ ください.

examples.ja: いくつですか。― ふたつです。
examples.en: How many? — Two.

examples.ja: メロンを ひとつ ください。
examples.en: One melon, please.

examples.ja: コーラと ジュースを ください。
examples.en: A cola and a juice, please.

examples.ja: おにぎりを ふたつと こうちゃを ひとつ ください。
examples.en: Two rice balls and one black tea, please.

sections.note: Six to ten are むっつ, ななつ, やっつ, ここのつ and とお; を is often dropped in speech.

sections.instruction: Match each word to the number of things.

items.explain: These words count things; the plain numbers いち, に, さん are for prices and phone numbers.

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each line.

items.ja: りんごは （　）ですか。― みっつです。
items.en: How many apples? — Three.
feedback: The answer is a count, みっつ, so the question is いくつ.
いくら asks a price; the answer would be in えん.
どれ asks which one; the answer would be これ or それ.

items.ja: みかんを （　） ください。
items.en: Four mandarins, please.
feedback: Things are counted with つ: four is よっつ.
よん is the plain number; counting mandarins needs よっつ.
やっつ is eight, not four.

items.ja: コロッケを ふたつ（　） コーラを ひとつ ください。
items.en: Two croquettes and one cola, please.
feedback: と joins the croquettes and the cola in one order.
も means “too”; it does not join two items in a list.
を already follows コーラ; the link between the items is と.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: Three hamburgers, please.
items.explain: The thing with を, then the number, then ください.

items.en: One sandwich and two puddings, please.
items.explain: Each thing has its own number, and と after the first number joins them.

sections.instruction: Choose what you would say.

items.prompt: At a café counter you want two rice balls and one black tea. What do you say?
choices: おにぎりを ふたつと こうちゃを ひとつ ください。
おにぎりを ひとつと こうちゃを ふたつ ください。
おにぎりと こうちゃを ふたつ ください。
feedback: Two after the rice balls, one after the tea, joined by と.
The numbers are swapped: this orders one rice ball and two teas.
One number at the end would mean two of the tea too.

items.prompt: The clerk asks: いくつですか。 You want five. What do you answer?
feedback: いくつ asks how many things: いつつ, five.
This is a price; いくつ asks how many.
ご is the plain number; things are counted with いつつ.

sections.instruction: Mark each statement ○ (true) or × (false).

items.statement: Tan asks the price of something away from him and the clerk.
items.explain: He says あれは いくらですか: あれ is away from them both.

items.statement: Tan orders two hamburgers.
items.explain: He says みっつ ください: three hamburgers.

items.statement: Tan catches the total the first time.
items.explain: He says もう いちど おねがいします, so he did not catch it.

sections.instruction: Complete the new conversation with words from the box.

lines.speaker: てんいん
lines.ja: いらっしゃいませ。

lines.speaker: マリー
lines.ja: すみません。（1）は いくらですか。

lines.speaker: てんいん
lines.ja: それは 160えんです。

lines.speaker: マリー
lines.ja: じゃあ、それを （2） ください。

lines.speaker: てんいん
lines.ja: はい、みっつですね。

lines.speaker: マリー
lines.ja: こうちゃ（3） ひとつ ください。

lines.speaker: てんいん
lines.ja: はい。（4） 680えんです。

items.en: Welcome. — Excuse me. How much is this one? — That’s 160 yen. — Okay, three of those, please. — Yes, three. — And one black tea too, please. — Sure. That’s 680 yen altogether.
items.explain: Marie points at the thing by her with これ, orders みっつ, adds the tea with も, and the clerk totals with ぜんぶで.

sections.instruction: Use everything from this lesson.

items.en: One melon and five lemons, please.
items.explain: と comes after the first thing’s number, ひとつ, before the second thing.

items.prompt: At a bag shop, you want the price of a bag on a high shelf, away from you and the clerk. What do you say?
choices: あれは いくらですか。
それは いくらですか。
これは いくらですか。
feedback: The bag is away from you both, so あれ.
それ is near the clerk, not up on a far shelf.
これ is near you.

items.prompt: At a fruit stall you want four apples. What do you say?
choices: りんごを よっつ ください。
りんごを よっつを ください。
りんごを よん ください。
feedback: を after りんご, then よっつ straight before ください.
を goes after the thing once, not after the number too.
よん is the plain number; apples are counted with よっつ.

items.en: Excuse me, how much is the popcorn?
items.explain: すみません gets attention, then the thing with は and いくらですか.

items.prompt: The clerk tells you: ジュースは 200えん、コーラは 150えんです。 You decide on the cola. What do you say?
choices: じゃあ、コーラに します。
じゃあ、コーラは します。
じゃあ、コーラは いくらですか。
feedback: に します after コーラ says the cola is your choice.
に します needs に; は does not mark a choice.
You already know the price; this asks it again.

items.stem: ただしければ ○、ちがえば ×。
items.statement: At a counter, いくつですか asks how much something costs.
items.explain: いくつ asks how many; いくら asks how much.

lessons.title: Which Floor?
lessons.goal: Ask where a department is in a store, and where to find the things you want on the floor.
lessons.context: A department store (デパート). Kim asks at the information desk for the glasses department, then asks a clerk on that floor where the watches are.

dialogue.speaker: キム
dialogue.ja: すみません。
dialogue.en: Excuse me.

dialogue.speaker: てんいん
dialogue.ja: はい、いらっしゃいませ。
dialogue.en: Yes, welcome.

dialogue.speaker: キム
dialogue.ja: めがねうりばは どこですか。
dialogue.en: Where is the glasses department?

dialogue.speaker: てんいん
dialogue.ja: めがねうりばは 6かいです。
dialogue.en: The glasses department is on the sixth floor.

dialogue.speaker: キム
dialogue.ja: 6かいですね。ありがとうございます。
dialogue.en: The sixth floor. Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: キム
dialogue.ja: すみません。とけいは どこに ありますか。
dialogue.en: (On the sixth floor) Excuse me. Where are the watches?

dialogue.speaker: てんいん
dialogue.ja: とけいですか。あちらです。めがねの うしろです。
dialogue.en: Watches? Over there. Behind the glasses.

dialogue.speaker: キム
dialogue.ja: あ、わかりました。どうも。
dialogue.en: Oh, I see. Thanks.

lessons.question: A clerk tells you: トイレは かいだんの まえです。 Where is the toilet?
feedback: まえ is in front: in front of the stairs.
Behind would be うしろ.
Next to would be となり.
lessons.focus: Ask where a department is with ～うりばは どこですか and understand the floor, 4かい or ちか. Ask where things are with ～は どこに ありますか and follow となり, まえ and うしろ.

sections.title: Asking where a department is
sections.pattern: ［N］は どこですか。― ［N］は ［number］かいです。
sections.explain: どこ asks where. In a store, ask for a department with ～うりば, and the answer gives the floor: 4かい is the fourth floor, and ちか the basement. なんがいですか asks for the floor itself.

examples.ja: とけいうりばは どこですか。― 5かいです。
examples.en: Where is the watch department? — On the fifth floor.

examples.ja: かさうりばは なんがいですか。― 2かいです。
examples.en: Which floor is the umbrella department on? — The second floor.

examples.ja: しょくひんうりばは ちかです。
examples.en: The food floor is in the basement.

sections.note: 3かい is read さんがい, like なんがい.

sections.instruction: Match each word to its meaning.

items.explain: くつした is くつ, shoes, plus した: what goes under them.

sections.instruction: Sort each word: something to wear, or food?

items.explain: The food is sold on the しょくひん floor; clothes and shoes are on the floors above.

sections.instruction: Choose what the underlined part means here.

items.prompt: You ask a clerk for the business shoes. She points and says this. What does the underlined part mean?
items.ja: ビジネスシューズは あちらです。
feedback: あちら, said while pointing, is “over there”.
Downstairs would be a floor, such as ちか.
Next to is となり.

items.prompt: The clerk tells you the floor, and you say this. What does it show?
items.ja: 4かいですね。わかりました。
feedback: わかりました says you have got the answer.
If you did not hear, you ask もう いちど おねがいします.
Sorry is すみません.

items.prompt: A shopper asks you this. What does she want to know?
items.ja: くつうりばは なんがいですか。
choices: Which floor the shoe department is on
feedback: なんがい asks which floor.
The price would be いくら.
How many would be いくつ.

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each line.

items.ja: すみません。めがねうりばは （　）ですか。
items.en: Excuse me. Where is the glasses department?
feedback: どこ asks where the glasses department is.
いくら asks a price, not a place.
だれ asks who.

items.ja: セーターうりばは 4（　）です。
items.en: The sweater department is on the fourth floor.
feedback: かい after 4 makes it the fourth floor.
つ counts things, not floors.
えん makes a price, not a floor.

items.ja: ネクタイうりばは （　）ですか。― 1かいです。
items.en: Which floor is the necktie department on? — The first floor.
feedback: The answer is a floor, so なんがい.
いくつ asks how many things.
どれ asks which one of several things.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: Excuse me. Where is the hat department?
items.explain: The department with は, then どこですか.

items.en: The food floor is in the basement.
items.explain: The department with は, then the place, ちか, and です.

sections.instruction: Look at the store guide and choose the answer.

items.prompt: A shopper asks the information desk: とけいうりばは どこですか。 What does the clerk answer?
card: 5かい … くつ・スニーカー
4かい … セーター・シャツ
1かい … ぼうし・くつした
feedback: The guide puts watches on 6かい.
5かい is shoes and sneakers.
ちか is the food floor.

items.prompt: You want socks. Using the guide, what do you ask the clerk?
card: 5かい … くつ・スニーカー
4かい … セーター・シャツ
1かい … ぼうし・くつした
choices: くつしたうりばは どこですか。
くつしたは いくらですか。
くつしたを ください。
feedback: You need the place first: くつしたうりばは どこですか.
This asks a price, not where they are.
This orders socks before you have found them.

items.prompt: The clerk answers your question: かばんうりばは 2かいです。 Which floor do you go to?
card: 5かい … くつ・スニーカー
4かい … セーター・シャツ
1かい … ぼうし・くつした
feedback: 2かい is the second floor, as the guide also shows.
4かい would be the fourth floor.
The basement is ちか.

sections.title: Asking where things are
sections.pattern: ［thing］は どこに ありますか。― ［N］の となり／まえ／うしろです。
sections.explain: To ask where a thing is, say ［thing］は どこに ありますか. The answer names a landmark with の and a position word: パンの となり, next to the bread. あちらです points the way.

examples.ja: ぎゅうにゅうは どこに ありますか。― やさいの まえです。
examples.en: Where is the milk? — In front of the vegetables.

examples.ja: ネクタイは どこに ありますか。― あちらです。シャツの うしろです。
examples.en: Where are the neckties? — Over there. Behind the shirts.

sections.note: Thank the clerk with ありがとうございます, or a lighter どうも.

sections.instruction: Choose the word that completes each line.

items.ja: すみません。バナナは どこに （　）か。
items.en: Excuse me. Where are the bananas?
feedback: どこに ありますか asks where a thing is.
どこに takes あります; どこですか has no に.
ください asks for something; this asks where.

items.ja: たまごは にく（　） となりです。
items.en: The eggs are next to the meat.
feedback: の links the meat to となり: next to the meat.
は marks the topic, たまご; it does not link にく to となり.
を marks what you ask for; it does not link a place word.

items.ja: くだものは やさいの （　）です。
items.en: The fruit is behind the vegetables.
feedback: うしろ is behind.
まえ is in front, not behind.
となり is next to, not behind.

sections.instruction: Put the tiles in order.

items.en: The fish is in front of the bread.
items.explain: The thing with は, the landmark with の, then the position word and です.

sections.instruction: Look at the shelf plan and choose the answer.

items.prompt: A shopper asks: ぶどうは どこに ありますか。 What does the clerk answer?
card: Back row: パン | ぎゅうにゅう | ぶどう
Front row: たまご | さかな | バナナ
choices: ぎゅうにゅうの となりです。
ぎゅうにゅうの まえです。
パンの となりです。
feedback: The grapes sit beside the milk in the back row.
In front of the milk is the fish.
Next to the bread is the milk, not the grapes.

items.prompt: Using the same plan, where are the eggs?
card: Back row: パン | ぎゅうにゅう | ぶどう
Front row: たまご | さかな | バナナ
choices: パンの うしろです。
バナナの となりです。
feedback: The eggs are in the front row, in front of the bread.
The bread is in the back row, so the eggs are not behind it.
The banana is at the other end, beside the fish.

items.prompt: A clerk tells you: トイレは あちらです。かいだんの となりです。 What do you say?
choices: トイレを ください。
feedback: You have the answer, so わかりました and a short どうも.
Staff say いらっしゃいませ to customers.
ください asks to be given a thing; you were asking the way.

sections.instruction: Mark each statement ○ (true) or × (false).

items.statement: The glasses department is on the sixth floor.
items.explain: The clerk says めがねうりばは 6かいです.

items.statement: The watches are in front of the glasses.
items.explain: The clerk says めがねの うしろです: behind the glasses.

items.statement: Kim does not understand the clerk on the sixth floor.
items.explain: Kim says わかりました: she understood.
